verdicts.reasoning: I traced this in the code; I did not run it. src/components/canvas/canvas-panel.tsx:1237 mounts `<div key={selectedVersion}>` around DesignEditor. onCommitted (1243-1255) appends `{version, content: "", origin: "edit"}`. The effect at 313-315 sets selectedVersion from artifact.currentVersion. versionContent at 369-370 is `find(...)?.content ?? artifact.content`, and "" is not nullish, so the editor remounts with content "". use-design-document.ts:167-180 then calls parseStoredDesignDocument(""), which throws 'Design document is not valid JSON' (migrations.ts:91-97), and design-editor.tsx:520-535 shows 'This design can’t be opened'. The path is reachable. Model output is stored with origin "generated" (artifacts-store.ts:59,86,117), and allocatesCheckpoint returns true when latest.origin !== "edit" (operations.ts:535), so the first user edit on a chat design always creates v2 and the route returns the new currentVersion (transactions/route.ts:52-53). It is worse than claimed. chat-view.tsx:1254-1262 stores the fake empty version in chat state, and nothing re-fetches the artifact on open (grep for /api/artifacts in chat-view and canvas-panel finds only export and save calls). Closing and reopening the Canvas therefore shows the same error until the conversation reloads. The version rail also offers a v2 that cannot be viewed. /design/[artifactId] is unaffected (design-workspace.tsx:215 passes setCurrentVersion).

export.ts:1195-1203: fire() only toggles `hidden` on roots. The interaction loop at 1075-1112 never reads interaction.transition, and grep of export.ts finds `transition` only in the handoff bundle (1710, 1804-1809). No unsupported.push mentions a transition. The default for every new interaction is dissolve 220ms (interactions-panel.tsx:54-60), so every exported navigation silently drops an authored transition. The panel note (179-182) says only that 'triggers' reach the export. Severity holds. As listed under missed, the HTML download drops even the unsupported notes the exporter does write.

export.ts:1204-1233 binds every node once at load. The delay branch (1216-1218) calls window.setTimeout immediately. The key branch (1211-1215) adds a document keydown listener, and fire() (1191-1203) navigates regardless of whether the source's .juno-root is hidden. Non-first roots are emitted hidden (1164). A delay on Screen 2 therefore fires while Screen 1 is showing, and it is never re-armed when Screen 2 is shown later. Scroll-into-view is fine, because a hidden root does not intersect.

The mapping is real. The labels say 'While hovering' and 'While pressed' (interactions-panel.tsx:64-65). press is counted as bindable (export.ts:1082-1088) and falls through to 'click' (1230-1231). hover is mouseenter only (1209-1210), and nothing reverts either one. The failure scenario is wrong, though: set-variant and open-overlay are not exported at all. They hit `unsupported.push(... interaction not represented)` and `continue` (1104-1106). The real impact is limited to navigate, open-url and play-animation. A hover→navigate never returns, a hover→open-url calls window.open on mouseenter (no user activation, so popup blockers refuse it), and a press→play fires on release and never reverses. That is a narrower fidelity gap than claimed, so I rate it low.

export.ts:1184-1188: `if (reverse) el.style.animationDirection = 'reverse';` has no else branch. The animationName reset (1184-1186) does not clear the inline direction, so every later forward play runs reversed. animationPlayState='running' is also written inline for every animation on the element (1188). That overrides the paused/:hover rules from buildMotionCss (1008-1025), so a hover-state animation on the same layer then runs without hover. The only test (tests/design-motion-export.test.ts:191-217) checks for the attribute string. Open/close with forward and reverse is the canonical use, so medium holds.

REPRODUCED with a scratch probe on the sign-in fixture. With an x track 0→100 on 'email' (an in-flow child of auto-layout 'card', layoutChild.absolute=false), the preview layout box stays at x=48 at t=1000. The export emits `0% { left: 24px } 100% { left: 124px }`. Cause: layout.ts:229-235 places in-flow children by the stack, while applyMotionValue writes node.x (motion-model.ts:374-377). The export positions everything absolutely (export.ts:512-513), and motionBase (728-737) deliberately applies the delta. propertyApplies (109-120) and the panel (536, 559-565) show no warning for this case.

REPRODUCED on 'card' (x=24, width 327). Tracks [x=0, scale 0.5] give x=81.75, width 163.5. Tracks [scale 0.5, x=0] give x=0, width 163.5. derivePreviewDocument applies tracks in array order (motion-model.ts:485-499). The scale case centres on the current geometry (400-416), and a later x track overwrites that centring. The export writes left plus `transform: scale()` about the centre, so its result is independent of track order and matches only the first ordering. setKeyframes appends new tracks (operations.ts:1551-1552).

REPRODUCED. Scale 2 on text 'title' gives width 279→558 but fontSize 16→16. The scale case in applyMotionValue (400-416) does not touch typography, and scaleSubtree (452-480) runs only for containers. Scale 2 on the 'button' frame gives label font 16→32 but cornerRadius stays 8. Stroke width and effects are not scaled either. The export uses `transform: scale()` (export.ts:915-925), which scales everything.

REPRODUCED. Keyframes 0→0, 1000→1, 1500→0.2 with durationMs 1000 export as `100% { opacity: 1; opacity: 0.2; ... }` with unsupported=[]. The preview reads 0.2 at 1500 because animationSpanMs is max(duration, last keyframe) (motion-model.ts:506-512), while percentOf clamps to [0,1] (export.ts:836). The Duration field lets you go below existing keyframes (motion-panel.tsx:410-418), and the keyframe Time field allows up to 600000 (745-753).

Computed with the real easedProgress. The default spring 180/20/1 reaches 0.706 at 150ms, 0.882 at 200ms and 1.020 at 300ms. 100/60/1 reaches 0.481 at 400ms. sampleTrack hands over to the next keyframe's value exactly at its time (motion-model.ts:329-343), and that is pinned by tests/design-motion.test.ts:122-133. A short spring segment therefore snaps 12-29% in one frame. The snap is a documented, tested design choice, but it is still visible on the button-press case. The export substitutes ease-out (export.ts:791-797). That note goes into `unsupported`, which for the HTML download never reaches the user (see missed). It survives only inside the handoff bundle JSON.

The window keydown handler (design-editor.tsx:410-421) passes whenever document.activeElement is inside rootRef, and MotionPanel is rendered inside that root (553, 812). Backspace/Delete then applies deleteNodes on the layer selection (476-482). The diamond is a <button> with only pointer handlers: it stops pointer propagation but has no onKeyDown (motion-panel.tsx:683-722). Only the playhead slider (630) and the number fields (918) stop key propagation. Clicking the diamond does not change the layer selection. deleteNodes also drops the layer's tracks (operations.ts:835-844). The auditor's two focus paths (Chromium focuses the clicked button; WKWebView keeps focus on the canvas) are inferred, not observed, but both end at deleteNodes. Keyboard focus reached via Tab (ux-4) does the same.

The per-frame chain is real. rAF setTimeMs (motion-panel.tsx:190-209) feeds onPreview (178-181), then setMotionPreview and a new previewDocument (design-editor.tsx:249-255). design-canvas.tsx:177 and 190-193 then re-run layoutPage and renderPageSvg and re-inject the SVG through dangerouslySetInnerHTML (1078). No design component is memoised. The failure scenario is inflated, though. On the web a document is capped at 200,000 serialized characters (store.ts:63). The sign-in fixture serializes at about 670 bytes per node, so a saveable document holds a few hundred nodes, not a few thousand. At that size the auditor's own measurement is about 1ms of compute plus an ~80KB innerHTML. It is an architectural inefficiency; stutter on reachable documents is unproven.

REPRODUCED. After add, tracks are [[title, opacity, 1]]. After applying the inverse from invertTransaction, they are [[title, opacity, 0]]. operations.ts:1555-1559 inverts a new track to `{...track, keyframes: []}`, not a removal. addTracks skips an existing nodeId+property (motion-panel.tsx:244-249). The row's own remove and add-keyframe controls can recover it, so low is right.

grep of motion-panel.tsx finds no zoom, snap, marquee, copy/paste, record/auto-key or loop-region code. timeFromPointer and offsetFor (307-319) map the full span to the lane width, rounded to 1ms, with no snapping. A spring segment differs only by bg-primary/50 vs /25 (671-674). rulerTicks loops `t < span` (840-847), so for span 1000 the ticks are 0-800 and there is no end tick.

The keyframe <button> (motion-panel.tsx:681-722) has only pointer handlers. Enter or Space fires a click that nothing handles, so keyboard users cannot select a keyframe, and the footer editor opens only for a selected one (742+). The aria-label is `Keyframe at ${ms} ms`, with no track or property. Worse, a Tab-focused diamond is inside the editor root, so Delete reaches the editor's deleteNodes handler (design-editor.tsx:476-482) and removes the selected layers.

This is the same finding as motion-15, confirmed there. The Mac fixed the equivalent library problem with DesktopDesignSurface (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:953-972, whose doc names the JSON-dump bug it fixed), but the web inline card still sends DESIGN to the sandbox's <pre> fallback.

missed.title: HTML prototype download drops its unsupported notes, so every limitation the exporter records is hidden from the user
missed.evidence: READ: the html case returns `download(result.content, result.fileName, result.mimeType)` (218-221). The download() helper (173-181) sets only Content-Type, Content-Disposition and Cache-Control. Only the PDF branch adds `X-Juno-Export-Notes` (213). The editor reads that header after the blob download (design-editor.tsx:335-339), so for HTML it is always null. exportHtmlPrototype's `unsupported` (export.ts:1244) reaches the user only inside the handoff bundle JSON (export.ts buildHandoffBundle, `unsupported: [...html.unsupported]`).
missed.failure_scenario: The exporter records several notes in `unsupported`: a spring substituted by ease-out (export.ts:791-797), a drag trigger (1089-1091), back/overlay/set-variant/set-variable actions that are not represented (1104-1106), timing conflicts, and rotation/scale filled in linearly. A designer who downloads the HTML prototype sees none of them; there is no toast. They believe the file is faithful, which undercuts the product's stated principle of 'reported rather than quietly approximated' (export.ts:707-709).

missed.title: Export menu in the Mac and iPhone hosted editor cannot work: it fetches /api from a file:// page whose CSP is connect-src 'none'
missed.evidence: READ: exportAs calls `fetch(`/api/design/${artifactId}/export?${query}`)` (298-304). The Export dropdown (656-681) is rendered unconditionally; it is not gated on transport or host. The host entry (src/components/design/host/main.tsx) passes a bridge transport but does not override export or fetch. The Mac loads the bundle with `loadFileURL` (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:121), and the bundle's index.html sets `connect-src 'none'` (scripts/build-design-editor.mjs INDEX_HTML). grep finds no WKUserScript or fetch shim in either native host, and no design export in the Mac app (grep of native/macOS/JunoDesktop/App).
missed.failure_scenario: On the Mac, the user opens a design, chooses Export → HTML prototype (or PNG, SVG, PDF, React, SwiftUI or the handoff bundle) and gets only an error toast (the fetch is refused). The same menu shows in the read-only iPhone editor. Since the HTML export is the only way to run a prototype (ux-0), Mac and iPhone users have no runnable prototype at all. I inferred this from CSP and origin rules; I did not run the app.
